PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = ThreeSat
3-SAT.

Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[l1, l2, l3], ...]}
  * Variables are 1..m. A literal is +v (v is true) or -v (v is false).
  * Every clause has exactly 3 literals on 3 different variables, so a
    clause may not repeat a variable or contain both v and -v.
  * Literal order inside a clause and clause order do not matter. The
    same clause may appear more than once.
  * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes every
clause contain at least one true literal.

Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is satisfiable (yes), for any m,
including m = 0. A formula with clauses needs m >= 3.

TARGET = OneInThreeSat
1-in-3-SAT (positive one-in-three satisfiability).

Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[a, b, c], ...]}
  * Variables are 1..m.
  * Every clause lists exactly 3 different variables, all as positive
    integers: negated literals are not allowed in this problem.
  * Variable order inside a clause and clause order do not matter. The
    same clause may appear more than once.
  * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes EXACTLY ONE
of the three variables in every clause true.

Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is yes, for any m, including
m = 0. A formula with clauses needs m >= 3.

WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-x4q06q3u

def require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise InvalidInstance(message)


def is_int(value: Any) -> bool:
    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)


def require_keys(instance: Any, keys: set[str]) -> None:
    require(isinstance(instance, dict), "instance must be a dict")
    require(
        set(instance) == keys,
        f"instance keys must be exactly {sorted(keys)}, got {sorted(instance)}",
    )


def require_int(value: Any, field: str, minimum: int | None = None) -> None:
    require(is_int(value), f"{field} must be an int")
    if minimum is not None:
        require(value >= minimum, f"{field} must be >= {minimum}")


def validate_graph(instance: Instance) -> None:
    """Check the "n" and "edges" fields of a graph instance."""
    n = instance.get("n")
    require_int(n, "n", minimum=0)
    edges = instance.get("edges")
    require(isinstance(edges, list), "edges must be a list")
    seen: set[frozenset[int]] = set()
    for edge in edges:
        require(
            isinstance(edge, list) and len(edge) == 2,
            f"each edge must be a list [u, v], got {edge!r}",
        )
        u, v = edge
        require(is_int(u) and is_int(v), f"edge endpoints must be ints, got {edge!r}")
        require(0 <= u < n and 0 <= v < n, f"edge {edge!r} has a vertex outside 0..{n - 1}")
        require(u != v, f"self-loop {edge!r} is not allowed")
        key = frozenset((u, v))
        require(key not in seen, f"duplicate edge {edge!r}")
        seen.add(key)

    """Check a DIMACS-style clause list over variables 1..num_vars."""
    require_int(num_vars, "num_vars", minimum=0)
    require(isinstance(clauses, list), "clauses must be a list")
    for clause in clauses:
        require(isinstance(clause, list), f"each clause must be a list, got {clause!r}")
        for literal in clause:
            require(is_int(literal), f"literals must be ints, got {literal!r}")
            require(
                literal != 0 and abs(literal) <= num_vars,
                f"literal {literal} is outside ±1..±{num_vars}",
            )

    assert isinstance(instance, dict)
    validate_graph(instance)
    require_int(instance["k"], "k")

    """Exactly 3 literals per clause on 3 different variables."""

    for clause in instance["clauses"]:

        require(
            len({abs(literal) for literal in clause}) == 3,
            f"clause {clause!r} must use 3 different variables",
        )

                all(literal > 0 for literal in clause),
                f"clause {clause!r} must contain only positive literals",
            )

def validate_set_system(instance: object, keys: set[str]) -> None:

    assert isinstance(instance, dict)
    universe_size = instance["universe_size"]
    require_int(universe_size, "universe_size", minimum=0)
    sets = instance["sets"]
    require(isinstance(sets, list), "sets must be a list")
    for subset in sets:
        require(isinstance(subset, list), f"each set must be a list, got {subset!r}")
        for element in subset:
            require(is_int(element), f"elements must be ints, got {element!r}")
            require(
                0 <= element < universe_size,
                f"element {element} is outside 0..{universe_size - 1}",
            )
        require(len(set(subset)) == len(subset), f"set {subset!r} repeats an element")


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validation helpers from benchmark/problems/numbers_common.py


def validate_numbers(numbers: object) -> None:
    require(isinstance(numbers, list), "numbers must be a list")
    assert isinstance(numbers, list)
    for number in numbers:
        require(is_int(number), f"numbers must be ints, got {number!r}")
        require(number >= 0, f"numbers must be >= 0, got {number}")

class ThreeSat:
    """3-SAT.

    Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[l1, l2, l3], ...]}
      * Variables are 1..m. A literal is +v (v is true) or -v (v is false).
      * Every clause has exactly 3 literals on 3 different variables, so a
        clause may not repeat a variable or contain both v and -v.
      * Literal order inside a clause and clause order do not matter. The
        same clause may appear more than once.
      * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

    Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes every
    clause contain at least one true literal.

    Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is satisfiable (yes), for any m,
    including m = 0. A formula with clauses needs m >= 3.
    """

    name = '3-SAT'

    @classmethod
    def validate(cls, instance: object) -> None:
        require_keys(instance, {"num_vars", "clauses"})
        assert isinstance(instance, dict)
        validate_cnf(instance["clauses"], instance["num_vars"])
        for clause in instance["clauses"]:
            require(len(clause) == 3, f"clause {clause!r} must have exactly 3 literals")
            require(
                len({abs(literal) for literal in clause}) == 3,
                f"clause {clause!r} must use 3 different variables",
            )


class OneInThreeSat:
    """1-in-3-SAT (positive one-in-three satisfiability).

    Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[a, b, c], ...]}
      * Variables are 1..m.
      * Every clause lists exactly 3 different variables, all as positive
        integers: negated literals are not allowed in this problem.
      * Variable order inside a clause and clause order do not matter. The
        same clause may appear more than once.
      * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

    Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes EXACTLY ONE
    of the three variables in every clause true.

    Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is yes, for any m, including
    m = 0. A formula with clauses needs m >= 3.
    """

    name = '1-in-3-SAT'

    @classmethod
    def validate(cls, instance: object) -> None:
        validate_three_literal_formula(instance, positive_only=True)

def find_or3(k, max_clauses):
    nvars = 3+k
    # candidate clauses: triples of distinct vars, any signs
    all_cl=[]
    for vt in it.combinations(range(nvars),3):
        for signs in it.product([1,-1],repeat=3):
            all_cl.append(tuple(zip(vt,signs)))
    aux_assigns=list(it.product([0,1],repeat=k))
    na=len(aux_assigns)
    xyz=list(it.product([0,1],repeat=3))
    def ev(assign,clause):
        s=0
        for (v,sg) in clause:
            s+= assign[v] if sg==1 else 1-assign[v]
        return s==1
    masks=[]
    for cl in all_cl:
        m=[]
        for x in xyz:
            mask=0
            for i,a in enumerate(aux_assigns):
                if ev(x+a,cl): mask|=1<<i
            m.append(mask)
        masks.append(m)
    full=(1<<na)-1
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)
    res=[None]
    def dfs(start,state,chosen):
        if state[0]==0 and all(state[i]!=0 for i in range(1,8)):
            res[0]=list(chosen); return True
        if len(chosen)>=max_clauses: return False
        for j in range(start,len(all_cl)):
            ns=[state[i]&masks[j][i] for i in range(8)]
            if ns[0]!=0: continue
            if any(ns[i]==0 for i in range(1,8)): continue
            chosen.append(j)
            if dfs(j+1,ns,chosen): return True
            chosen.pop()
        return False
    dfs(0,[full]*8,[])
    if res[0] is None: return None
    return [all_cl[j] for j in res[0]]

for k in [2,3]:
    r=find_or3(k,7)
    print("k=",k,"found" if r else "none")
    if r: print(r); break

import itertools as it, sys

def find_or3(k, max_clauses):
    nvars=3+k
    all_cl=[]
    for vt in it.combinations(range(nvars),3):
        for signs in it.product([1,-1],repeat=3):
            all_cl.append(tuple(zip(vt,signs)))
    aux=list(it.product([0,1],repeat=k))
    na=len(aux)
    xyz=list(it.product([0,1],repeat=3))
    def ev(assign,cl):
        s=0
        for (v,sg) in cl:
            s+= assign[v] if sg==1 else 1-assign[v]
        return s==1
    masks=[]
    for cl in all_cl:
        m=[]
        for x in xyz:
            mask=0
            for i,a in enumerate(aux):
                if ev(x+a,cl): mask|=1<<i
            m.append(mask)
        masks.append(tuple(m))
    full=(1<<na)-1
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)
    res=[None]
    def dfs(start,state,chosen):
        if state[0]==0 and all(state[i]!=0 for i in range(1,8)):
            res[0]=list(chosen); return True
        if len(chosen)>=max_clauses: return False
        for j in range(start,len(all_cl)):
            ns=tuple(state[i]&masks[j][i] for i in range(8))
            if any(ns[i]==0 for i in range(1,8)): continue
            chosen.append(j)
            if dfs(j+1,ns,chosen): return True
            chosen.pop()
        return False
    dfs(0,[full]*8,[])
    if res[0] is None: return None
    return [all_cl[j] for j in res[0]]

for k in [2,3]:
    r=find_or3(k,7)
    print("k=",k,"found" if r else "none")
    if r: print(r); break
EOF

import itertools as it
from collections import deque
import sys

def find_or3(k, max_clauses, state_cap=3000000):
    nvars=3+k
    all_cl=[]
    for vt in it.combinations(range(nvars),3):
        for signs in it.product([1,-1],repeat=3):
            all_cl.append(tuple(zip(vt,signs)))
    aux=list(it.product([0,1],repeat=k))
    na=len(aux)
    xyz=list(it.product([0,1],repeat=3))
    def ev(assign,cl):
        s=0
        for (v,sg) in cl:
            s+= assign[v] if sg==1 else 1-assign[v]
        return s==1
    masks=[]
    for cl in all_cl:
        m=[]
        for x in xyz:
            mask=0
            for i,a in enumerate(aux):
                if ev(x+a,cl): mask|=1<<i
            m.append(mask)
        masks.append(tuple(m))
    full=(1<<na)-1
    start=(full,)*8
    seen={start:()}
    q=deque([start])
    while q:
        st=q.popleft()
        path=seen[st]
        if st[0]==0 and all(st[i]!=0 for i in range(1,8)):

            if any(ns[i]==0 for i in range(1,8)): continue
            if ns in seen: continue
            if len(seen)>state_cap: return "CAP"
            seen[ns]=path+(j,)
            q.append(ns)
    return None

import itertools as it
from collections import deque
import sys

def find_or3(k, max_clauses, state_cap=3000000):
    nvars=3+k
    all_cl=[]
    for vt in it.combinations(range(nvars),3):
        for signs in it.product([1,-1],repeat=3):
            all_cl.append(tuple(zip(vt,signs)))
    aux=list(it.product([0,1],repeat=k))
    na=len(aux)
    xyz=list(it.product([0,1],repeat=3))
    def ev(assign,cl):
        s=0
        for (v,sg) in cl:
            s+= assign[v] if sg==1 else 1-assign[v]
        return s==1
    masks=[]
    for cl in all_cl:
        m=[]
        for x in xyz:
            mask=0
            for i,a in enumerate(aux):
                if ev(x+a,cl): mask|=1<<i
            m.append(mask)
        masks.append(tuple(m))
    full=(1<<na)-1
    start=(full,)*8
    seen={start:()}
    q=deque([start])
    while q:
        st=q.popleft()
        path=seen[st]
        if st[0]==0 and all(st[i]!=0 for i in range(1,8)):
            return [all_cl[j] for j in path]
        if len(path)>=max_clauses: continue
        for j in range(len(all_cl)):
            ns=tuple(st[i]&masks[j][i] for i in range(8))
            if ns[0]!=0: continue
            if any(ns[i]==0 for i in range(1,8)): continue
            if ns in seen: continue
            if len(seen)>state_cap: return "CAP"
            seen[ns]=path+(j,)
            q.append(ns)
    return None

for k in [4,5]:
    r=find_or3(k, 10)
    print("k=",k, r if isinstance(r,str) else ("found" if r else "none"))
    if r and not isinstance(r,str):
        print(r); break

import itertools as it
from collections import deque

def find_or3(k, max_clauses, state_cap=5000000):
    nvars=3+k
    all_cl=[]
    for vt in it.combinations(range(nvars),3):
        for signs in it.product([1,-1],repeat=3):
            all_cl.append(tuple(zip(vt,signs)))
    aux=list(it.product([0,1],repeat=k))
    na=len(aux)
    xyz=list(it.product([0,1],repeat=3))
    def ev(assign,cl):
        s=0
        for (v,sg) in cl:
            s+= assign[v] if sg==1 else 1-assign[v]
        return s==1
    masks=[]
    for cl in all_cl:
        m=[]
        for x in xyz:
            mask=0
            for i,a in enumerate(aux):
                if ev(x+a,cl): mask|=1<<i
            m.append(mask)
        masks.append(tuple(m))
    full=(1<<na)-1
    start=(full,)*8
    seen={start:()}
    q=deque([start])
    while q:
        st=q.popleft()
        path=seen[st]
        if st[0]==0 and all(st[i]!=0 for i in range(1,8)):
            return [all_cl[j] for j in path]
        if len(path)>=max_clauses: continue
        for j in range(len(all_cl)):
            ns=tuple(st[i]&masks[j][i] for i in range(8))
            # prune only if some good assignment becomes impossible
            if any(ns[i]==0 for i in range(1,8)): continue
            if ns in seen: continue
            if len(seen)>state_cap: return "CAP"
            seen[ns]=path+(j,)
            q.append(ns)
    return None

for k in [2,3]:
    r=find_or3(k, 8)
    print("k=",k, r if isinstance(r,str) else ("found" if r else "none"))
    if r and not isinstance(r,str):
        print(r); break

import itertools as it
from collections import deque

def find_or3(k, max_clauses, state_cap=5000000):
    nvars=3+k
    all_cl=[]
    for vt in it.combinations(range(nvars),3):
        for signs in it.product([1,-1],repeat=3):
            all_cl.append(tuple(zip(vt,signs)))
    aux=list(it.product([0,1],repeat=k))
    na=len(aux)
    xyz=list(it.product([0,1],repeat=3))
    def ev(assign,cl):
        s=0
        for (v,sg) in cl:
            s+= assign[v] if sg==1 else 1-assign[v]
        return s==1
    masks=[]
    for cl in all_cl:
        m=[]
        for x in xyz:
            mask=0
            for i,a in enumerate(aux):
                if ev(x+a,cl): mask|=1<<i
            m.append(mask)
        masks.append(tuple(m))
    full=(1<<na)-1
    start=(full,)*8
    seen={start:()}
    q=deque([start])
    while q:
        st=q.popleft()
        path=seen[st]
        if st[0]==0 and all(st[i]!=0 for i in range(1,8)):
            return [all_cl[j] for j in path]
        if len(path)>=max_clauses: continue
        for j in range(len(all_cl)):
            ns=tuple(st[i]&masks[j][i] for i in range(8))
            # prune only if some good assignment becomes impossible
            if any(ns[i]==0 for i in range(1,8)): continue
            if ns in seen: continue
            if len(seen)>state_cap: return "CAP"
            seen[ns]=path+(j,)
            q.append(ns)
    return None

for k in [2,3]:
    r=find_or3(k, 8)
    print("k=",k, r if isinstance(r,str) else ("found" if r else "none"))
    if r and not isinstance(r,str):
        print(r); break
EOF

import itertools as it
R=[(1,0,0),(0,1,0),(0,0,1)]

def preserves(f,k):
    # f: tuple of k bits -> bit
    for tup in it.product(R,repeat=k):
        out=tuple(f(*[tup[j][i] for j in range(k)]) for i in range(3))
        if out not in R: return False

for bits in it.product([0,1],repeat=4):
    f=lambda a,b,bits=bits: bits[a*2+b]
    if preserves(f,2):
        print("  ",bits)

cnt=0
for bits in it.product([0,1],repeat=8):
    f=lambda a,b,c,bits=bits: bits[a*4+b*2+c]
    if preserves(f,3):
        print("  ",bits); cnt+=1
print("count",cnt)
EOF

    cmask=[]

    # enumerate witness choices: for each good g, choose aux index
    results=[]

import itertools as it

def find_gadget(k, good_set, bad_set, max_report=5):
    # vars: 0,1,2 = x,y,z ; 3..3+k-1 aux. Clauses: triples distinct vars, any signs.
    nvars=3+k
    clauses=[]
    for vt in it.combinations(range(nvars),3):
        for signs in it.product([1,-1],repeat=3):
            clauses.append(tuple(zip(vt,signs)))
    aux=list(it.product([0,1],repeat=k))
    def ev(assign,cl):
        s=0
        for (v,sg) in cl:
            s+= assign[v] if sg==1 else 1-assign[v]
        return s==1
    # precompute for each clause and each (g, aux) whether satisfied
    # good_set, bad_set are lists of xyz tuples
    # For witness search: for each good g choose aux w_g
    good=list(good_set)
    bad=list(bad_set)
    # clause satisfaction: sat[cl][g][w]
    # We'll represent clause as frozenset of (g, w) pairs satisfied
    # To speed: for each clause, a bitmask over (good index, aux index)
    G=len(good); A=len(aux)
    # For each clause, mask over good*aux
    cmask=[]
    for cl in clauses:
        m=0
        for gi,g in enumerate(good):
            for wi,w in enumerate(aux):
                if ev(g+w,cl):
                    m|=1<<(gi*A+wi)
        cmask.append(m)
    # bad satisfiability: for each clause, set of aux satisfying bad
    badmask=[]
    for cl in clauses:
        m=0
        for wi,w in enumerate(aux):
            if ev(tuple(bad[0])+w,cl):  # bad_set assumed single
                m|=1<<wi
        badmask.append(m)
    # enumerate witness choices: for each good g, choose aux index
    results=[]
    for choice in it.product(range(A),repeat=G):
        # intersection: clause must be satisfied by all (g, choice[g])
        full=(1<<(G*A))-1
        inter=full
        for gi in range(G):
            # mask of clauses satisfied at (gi, choice[gi]) : need per-clause
            pass
        # simpler: iterate clauses, check
        chosen=[]
        for ci,cl in enumerate(clauses):
            ok=True
            for gi in range(G):
                if not ev(good[gi]+aux[choice[gi]], cl):
                    ok=False;break
            if ok: chosen.append(ci)
        # check bad unsatisfiable
        sat_bad=False
        for wi,w in enumerate(aux):
            if all(ev(tuple(bad[0])+w, clauses[ci]) for ci in chosen):
                sat_bad=True;break
        if not sat_bad:
            results.append((choice,chosen))
            if len(results)>=max_report: return results
    return results
